questions.text: What exactly does "Place order" receive and who calls it? Does it create an Order record first, and with what status?
What does "Reserve stock" do in Inventory: what is stored, and what does Place order do if there is not enough stock?
Who starts the 10 minute reservation timer, and what happens to the order and the reservation when it expires?
What does "Take payment" send to the provider, and does it wait for an answer or just continue until the webhook arrives?
What does the "Payment webhook" contain, and which service receives it? How is it checked as genuine?
How does "dedupe" work: what is the key, and where is it stored?
questions.about: Webhooks can be late or duplicated, so dedupe

questions.text: What does "Confirm order" change, and in which DB? What happens if payment fails or is declined?
The diagram shows Confirm order leading to both Clear cart and Refund. When does each happen, and how does the late-payment case (re-reserve, else refund and cancel) fit into the arrows?
What is the event that clears the cart, who publishes it, and what happens if Cart never receives it?

answers.text: Order service receives Place order from the customer's client. It reads the cart over HTTP, saves an order with the snapshot of lines and prices, status PENDING, then starts the flow. Chosen because Order must own the snapshot.

Inventory saves one reservation (order id, all lines, expires_at = now + 10 min) in a single transaction, all-or-nothing. If any line is short, it saves nothing and returns the short items. Order then sets OUT_OF_STOCK, requests no payment, tells the customer, and leaves the cart alone.

Inventory starts and owns the timer via expires_at on the reservation, plus a periodic sweep that returns unclaimed lapsed stock. The order is not notified or changed; it learns of it only when a payment result arrives and the claim fails or succeeds.
Payment sends the amount and order id as the idempotency key. It does not wait for the outcome: it returns at once and Order sets AWAITING_PAYMENT until the webhook result arrives.

The webhook carries the provider event id, the order id (payment reference) and the outcome, and Payment receives it. The brief does not say how it is authenticated; I assume the provider's signature with a shared secret and listed it under open questions.

Key is the provider's event id, stored in Payment's DB with a unique constraint. A repeat finds the id already stored and is ignored. Chosen because the provider sends the same id on redelivery. Added to the diagram step 4.

On PaymentSucceeded, Order asks Inventory to claim, then sets CONFIRMED in the Order DB. On PaymentDeclined, Order sets PAYMENT_FAILED, releases the reservation in Inventory, and leaves the cart untouched so the customer can retry.

The diagram was wrong: Confirm did not lead to Refund. Now Claim is the branch point. Claim ok leads to CONFIRMED then Clear cart. Claim fails (hold lapsed and stock sold) leads to CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, email and full refund. Claim also covers the 're-reserve' case: a lapsed hold is still claimed if stock is free.

Order publishes OrderConfirmed after saving CONFIRMED; Cart consumes it and empties the cart, which is harmless if repeated. If Cart never receives it, the broker redelivers; whether Order uses an outbox to avoid losing the publish is listed as an open question.

questions.text: Where does the customer enter card details, and what does Payment send to the provider that identifies the card? What does Payment return to Order when it returns at once?
If the provider call itself fails or times out in step 3, what status does the order end in, and what happens to the reservation?
questions.about: 3. ORDER asks PAYMENT to charge (Failure handling)

questions.text: If the webhook never arrives, what happens to the order, the reservation and the customer? Does anything check on the payment?
How does Order find the right order when PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined arrives, and what does it do if the same event is delivered twice or the order is already CONFIRMED or cancelled?
What does claim change in Inventory (reservation status, stock counts)? When a lapsed hold is claimed, how does Inventory decide stock is still free?
If Order crashes or Inventory is unreachable after PaymentSucceeded but before CONFIRMED is saved, what happens? Is the claim call safe to repeat?
When the customer retries after a decline, is it a new order or the same one? Is the order id the same idempotency key, and what happens to the old reservation?
How does the customer find out the order was cancelled and refunded, and what ensures the refund happens if Order fails after setting CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK but before asking Payment?

answers.text: Card details are entered in the provider's hosted form or SDK in the browser, which returns a one-time payment token. The client sends the token with Place order. Payment sends the token, amount and order id (as idempotency key) to the provider, so card data never touches our services. Payment returns a payment id at once. Added to Terms, step 1, step 3 and the diagram.

Order stays AWAITING_PAYMENT and repeats the call, which is safe because the idempotency key is the order id. After a fixed number of tries it sets PAYMENT_FAILED and releases the reservation. If the charge did go through, the late success is refunded. The try count is left open. Added to the step 3 row.

The brief does not say. My proposal is that Payment asks the provider for the payment's status once 30 minutes (the stated maximum) have passed without a webhook, and handles the answer like a webhook. The reservation lapses meanwhile and the customer sees awaiting payment. I do not know whether the provider offers a status lookup, so it is listed under open questions. Added to the step 4 row.

Both events carry the order id, and Order looks the order up by it. Only an order in AWAITING_PAYMENT acts on an event. A repeat for a CONFIRMED or cancelled order is ignored, and a success for an order already PAYMENT_FAILED is refunded. Chosen because the broker delivers at least once. Added to the step 5 row.

Reserving lowers the available count. Claim marks the reservation CLAIMED. If the reservation still exists, the stock is already set aside. If the sweep has returned the stock, Inventory checks in one transaction that every line's available count covers the order and lowers the counts, otherwise the claim fails. Claiming twice succeeds. Added as the Claim paragraph and a Terms line.

The PaymentSucceeded event is only acknowledged after CONFIRMED (or the cancel path) is saved, so a crash or an unreachable Inventory means redelivery and a retried claim. Claim is safe to repeat. Added to the Terms (Events) and the step 5 row.

A retry is a new order with a new order id, so a new idempotency key. The old order stays PAYMENT_FAILED and its reservation was released on the decline. The cart was left untouched, so the customer simply presses Place order again. Added to the step 1 row.

The customer gets an email and the order page shows the final status. To avoid losing the refund, Order now asks Payment for the refund first and sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK afterwards. If it crashes in between, the event is redelivered, the claim fails again, and the repeated refund request is harmless because the refund is keyed by order id. Cost is a possible duplicate email, noted as open. Changed the diagram node and step 8 row.

questions.text: Does the customer's Place order request stay open through steps 1 to 3, and what does the customer see when it returns?
If Order crashes after saving PENDING but before or during the reserve call, what happens to that order? Does anything pick it up again?
Who counts the charge tries and does the repeating, the Order service itself or something else? What drives each retry?
What does Order get back when it asks for the refund: confirmation that the refund happened, or only that the request was saved? What does Order set CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK on?
questions.about: 8. PAYMENT saves refund row first, then calls provider

questions.text: What does release do in Inventory to the reservation status and the available count? What if the reservation was already swept or claimed?
questions.about: Declined: ORDER tells INVENTORY to release the reservation

questions.text: When a late success arrives for an order already PAYMENT_FAILED and is refunded, what status does the order end in and does the customer get told?

answers.text: No. Place order returns once step 3 has handed the charge to Payment, which returns at once. The customer gets the order id and status AWAITING_PAYMENT (or OUT_OF_STOCK with the short items), and the order page shows later changes. Chosen because the outcome can take up to 30 minutes. Added to the step 3 row and diagram node.

As written before, nothing picked it up. Now a periodic check in Order sets orders still PENDING after 10 minutes to FAILED. No charge was requested, and any reservation lapses by itself, so nothing needs undoing. The customer presses Place order again. Added to the step 1 row.

Order itself counts the tries and repeats. A periodic check in Order picks up orders in AWAITING_PAYMENT that have no payment id yet and calls Payment again with the same order id. After a fixed number of tries (number undecided) it sets PAYMENT_FAILED and releases. Chosen as the simplest option with no new service. Added to the step 3 row.

Order gets back only that the request was saved (refund row PENDING). It sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK on that answer. The provider refund finishes later through Payment's retry, so the email says the refund is on its way. Chosen because Payment owns refund delivery and the refund is never dropped. Added to the step 8 row and Customer notice.

Release marks the reservation RELEASED and raises the available counts by its lines. If it was already swept or released, release does nothing and succeeds, so no double increase. Release is sent only after a decline or failed charge, which is before any claim, so a claimed reservation is not an expected case. Added as a Terms line.

The order stays PAYMENT_FAILED. Order asks Payment for a full refund and emails the customer that the payment was refunded. Chosen because the order was already ended as a payment failure, and CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK would be untrue. Added to the step 5 row.

questions.text: In step 4, Payment stores the event id and then publishes the event. If Payment crashes after storing the id but before publishing, the provider's redelivery is skipped as a repeat. Does the order ever get its PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined then?
questions.about: 4. Provider webhook reaches PAYMENT: check signature, skip if event id already stored, else store id and publish

answers.text: No, with the old order of steps the event could be lost: the id was stored first, so the provider's redelivery was skipped as a repeat. I changed step 4 to publish first, then store the event id, then reply 200. A crash before the reply makes the provider redeliver, and the event is published again. That is safe because Order acts only on an order in AWAITING_PAYMENT and ignores repeats on finished orders, and the broker already delivers at least once. Chosen because it needs no outbox or new mechanism. If the publish itself fails, Payment replies with an error and the provider redelivers. The 30-minute status lookup is a further backstop.

teachbacks.text:
1. Customer presses Place order; the client sends only a one-time payment token (card details went to the provider's own form, never to us). Order reads the cart from Cart over HTTP, saves a new order with a snapshot of lines and prices in its own DB, status PENDING. Every press makes a new order id. If Cart is unreachable, checkout fails and nothing needs undoing. If Order crashes while PENDING, a periodic check in Order sets it to FAILED after 10 minutes; nothing was charged and any reservation lapses by itself. The customer presses Place order again.

2. Order asks Inventory (HTTP) to reserve all lines. Inventory's DB holds stock counts and reservations; it saves one all-or-nothing reservation (order id, lines, expires_at 10 minutes, status) and lowers available counts. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, no payment happens, Order sets OUT_OF_STOCK, the customer sees the short items and the cart is untouched. If Inventory is unreachable, the order fails and the cart is untouched.

3. Order asks Payment (HTTP) to charge. Payment saves a payment row in its DB and calls the provider with the token, the amount and the order id as idempotency key. Payment returns a payment id at once, without waiting for the outcome. Order sets AWAITING_PAYMENT and Place order returns to the customer with the order id and that status. The order page shows later changes. If the call to Payment or the provider fails or times out, the order stays AWAITING_PAYMENT, and Order's periodic check repeats the charge call for orders with no payment id yet (safe because the same order id is the same provider key). After a fixed number of tries Order sets PAYMENT_FAILED and releases the reservation. A success arriving later is refunded.

4. The provider calls Payment's webhook, within seconds or up to 30 minutes later. Payment checks the signature (a bad signature is rejected), publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined on the broker, then stores the event id (in Payment's DB), then replies 200. If the event id is already stored, it replies 200 and publishes nothing. If Payment crashes before replying, the provider redelivers and the event is published again, which is harmless because Order only acts on AWAITING_PAYMENT orders. If no webhook arrives in 30 minutes, Payment asks the provider for the payment status and handles the answer as if it were the webhook.

5. Order receives the event (it carries the order id) and finds the order. Only an order in AWAITING_PAYMENT acts; a repeat on a finished order is ignored. Delivery is at-least-once and Order acknowledges only after finishing, so a crash or unreachable Inventory means redelivery.
 a. Declined: Order sets PAYMENT_FAILED and tells Inventory to release the reservation (Inventory marks it RELEASED and raises the counts; a no-op if already swept or released). The cart is untouched and the customer can retry with a fresh order.
 b. Succeeded: Order asks Inventory to claim. Inventory marks the reservation CLAIMED. If the hold is live, or lapsed but not yet swept, the stock is already set aside. If the sweep returned the stock, Inventory checks in one transaction that every line's available count covers the order and then lowers the counts; if any line does not cover it, the claim fails. Claiming an already claimed reservation succeeds, so repeats are safe.
 c. Side case: success arrives for an order already PAYMENT_FAILED. Order asks for a full refund, leaves the status PAYMENT_FAILED and emails the customer that the payment was refunded.
 Separately, Inventory alone owns the 10 minute timer. A periodic sweep returns unclaimed lapsed reservations to stock and Order is not told. Order learns the outcome only when the claim is tried.

6. Claim ok: Order sets CONFIRMED and publishes OrderConfirmed.

7. Cart consumes OrderConfirmed and empties the cart. If Cart never gets it, the cart stays full, the customer sees that, and the broker redelivers. Clearing twice is harmless.

8. Claim fails (stock gone): Order asks Payment over HTTP for a full refund keyed by order id (a repeat finds the existing refund row). Payment saves a refund row first and answers immediately, before calling the provider. Order then sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and emails the customer that the refund is on its way. The order page shows the final status. Payment then calls the provider; on failure the row stays PENDING and is retried until it succeeds, with an alert after repeated failures, and it is never dropped. If Order crashes after asking but before saving the cancel, the event is redelivered, the claim fails again and the repeated refund request is harmless.
gaps: How the client learns the order outcome after Place order returns: the order page 'shows later changes' but the mechanism (polling, push) and how the customer is told about a decline or PAYMENT_FAILED is not stated.

Whether Order's periodic check for no-payment-id orders is what retries the charge, but how many tries, the retry timing, and how it distinguishes a not-yet-attempted order from one whose payment id was never returned are not decided.
How Order finds the order from the payment event is stated (order id), but how Payment learns which order a webhook belongs to (provider payload fields) is not stated.
Who sends the cancellation/refund email and how, and how duplicates are avoided, is undecided (open question).
Whether Order reliably publishes OrderConfirmed after saving CONFIRMED is undecided (no outbox); a crash between them leaves the cart full with no stated recovery.
Whether the provider status lookup used when no webhook arrives exists is unconfirmed, so the 30 minute no-webhook path may not work.
What happens to an order stuck in AWAITING_PAYMENT if the status lookup also returns nothing or the order has a payment id but no result ever arrives is not stated.
What happens to the reservation and order if the refund path is taken after a failure of the claim because Inventory is unreachable for a long time: only 'redelivered' is stated, no limit.
What the authentic webhook signature method is is unconfirmed (open question).

How the OUT_OF_STOCK or declined customer flow gets short items shown beyond 'customer sees short items' is not detailed, and how a stale PENDING order that already has a live reservation is cleaned up other than lapse is not stated.
